name: biceps tendinopathy overview
title: Anterior shoulder pain: decide whether it is the long head of the biceps tendon (tendinopathy or a frank tear, diagnosed mostly by examination and treated with active physiotherapy) or a neighbour: rotator cuff tendinopathy or subacromial bursitis (ultrasound), a SLAP labral tear (MR arthrogram), arthritis, or pain referred from the neck or viscera

root.title: Anterior shoulder pain: is it the LONG HEAD OF BICEPS, or something next to it?
lines: onset: ACUTE (tear or inflammation) or CHRONIC (degeneration, overuse)

groups.title: Its neighbours, or pain from elsewhere
lines: all can give anterior shoulder pain

head: h
Proximal biceps tendinopathy
overuse to inflammation to a partial or complete tear
pres: • tender over the tendon in the intertubercular groove
• worse with shoulder + elbow flexion, forearm SUPINATED
tx: 1 · Educate: most are chronic and improve conservatively
2 · Physiotherapy, the mainstay: ACTIVE therapy · rest from overhead · analgesia

head: h
Rotator cuff tendinopathy · subacromial bursitis
the tendon lies beside the cuff tendons
pres: Lives right beside the biceps tendon
inv: sees the cuff tendons AND the bursa at the same time

head: h
Labral tear (SLAP lesion)
the tendon starts on the superior labrum
inv: if a SLAP lesion is suspected

head: h
Arthritis or referred pain
• shoulder or acromioclavicular (AC) joint arthritis
• cervical radiculopathy · facet joint · visceral
pres: • C4 or C5: can give shoulder pain
• C8: pain or tingling in the HAND, so LOW on the list
tx: See the SHOULDER and BACK & NECK charts
